name: WA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+22) in the Seattle suburbs
Long-serving incumbent Adam Smith with a large financial edge
Challenger Doug Basler raised only about $12,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price Smith near 97% to win
model.rationale: Adam Smith holds a D+22 district, a two-decade incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of roughly $1.9 million to $12,000, while markets price him at about 97%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability, the fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win.
model.watch: A surprise surge in challenger fundraising or outside spending, or an unusually low-turnout special dynamic, could narrow the margin, though nothing in the current evidence suggests that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Washington's 9th District, covering parts of the Seattle metro area, leans heavily Democratic with a partisan advantage of about 22 points. Adam Smith, the incumbent since the 1990s, advanced to the general election and holds a commanding financial position, with roughly $1.9 million raised and $870,000 on hand. His Republican challenger, Doug Basler, has raised only about $12,000 and has drawn no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets put Smith's chances near 97%. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap makes this one of the safest Democratic holds on the House map this cycle, with the main question being the size of the victory margin rather than the winner.
